slot.brief: A force applied at a point on a rigid body with given r and F vectors; compute torque as cross product and identify the component tending to rotate about a specified axis.

stem: A force $mathbf{F}=(1mathbf{i}+3mathbf{j}+2mathbf{k})$ N acts at position $mathbf{r}=(2mathbf{i}-mathbf{j}+mathbf{k})$ m relative to the origin. Find the signed component of torque along the positive direction $hat{mathbf{n}}=(mathbf{i}+2mathbf{j}+2mathbf{k})/3$.

verdicts.working: \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(-5,-3,7)\) N·m. Then \(\boldsymbol\tau\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}=(-5-6+14)/3=1\) N·m.

working:
$\boldsymbol{\tau}=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(-5\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+7\mathbf k)\ \text{N m}$
$\tau_n=\boldsymbol{\tau}\cdot(\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)/3=(-5-6+14)/3=1\ \text{N m}$

Independent check: \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(-5,-3,7)\) N·m. Then \(\boldsymbol\tau\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}=(-5-6+14)/3=1\) N·m.
solution:
The torque is $$\boldsymbol{\tau}=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(-5\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+7\mathbf k)\,\text{N m}$.
$$$\tau_n=\boldsymbol{\tau}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}=\frac{-5-6+14}{3}=1\,\text{N$ m}$$
